BiblicalUsage: Rain is God's gift and God's tool in Israel's story. Moses promises the early rain and the latter rain in their season if Israel obeys, and Solomon prays that when heaven is shut up for sin, God will hear and send rain again. Elijah announces the end of three years without rain, Zechariah tells the people to ask the LORD for rain, and the psalm pictures the king coming down like rain on mown grass.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rain teaches us how dependent we are: no one in Israel could make it rain, and no one can make grace fall either. When God withholds rain it is a call to repent, and when He sends it, it is a reminder that He alone opens heaven. I hold that the latter rain is still the picture of what God does when His people ask.
